 3                                              I.       INTRODUCTION
 4
 5   Q.      PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND WHO YOU ARE TESTIFYING ON BEHALF

 6            OF IN THIS PROCEEDING.

 7   A.      My name is Barbara Maddox. I am testifying on behalf of my husband, Rodger (Roddy)

 8           Maddox, and me.1


 9   Q.      PLEASE STATE YOUR ADDRESS.

10   A.      We are the landowners in Tract Nos. 1500, 1501, and 1502 located in San Saba and Llano

11            Counties, Texas. Our mailing address is P.O. Box 7, Cherokee, Texas 76832. Our physical

12            address is 291 CR 388, Cherokee, Texas 76832.

13   Q.      HAVE YOU EVER TESTIFIED BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION

14            OF TEXAS ("COMMISSION")?

15   A.      No, I have not.

16   Q.      WAS       THIS      TESTIMONY            PREPARED          BY    YOU       OR     UNDER        YOUR

17            SUPERVISION?

18   A.      Yes.

19                                   II.     PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY

20   Q.      WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY IN THIS PROCEEDING?

21   A.      Roddy and I oppose any route for the Oncor/LCRA's 765kV transmission line that includes

22           Link J33. The purpose of my testimony is to explain our concerns and why our concerns

 2            line.

 3                                  III.     OUR FAMILY AND OUR PROPERTY

 4   Q.    TELL THE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES AND COMMISSION ABOUT YOU

 5         AND YOUR FAMILY.

 6   A.    Roddy and I were both raised in Cherokee, Texas and we both graduated from Cherokee

 7         High School. Cherokee, Texas is just north of our property. Roddy furthered his education

 8         at Howard Payne College on a football scholarship and I went to Nixon Clay Business School

 9         in Austin, Texas. After we got married, Roddy came back to Cherokee High School to coach

10         and teach for thirty-five (35) years. I became an Administrative Secretary in the area for

11         thirty (30) years. Our lives together were built on hard work. At the time we were married,

12         we had a dream - Maddox Ranch - and we worked hard to accomplish that dream.

13   Q.    PLEASE TELL US ABOUT THE MADDOX RANCH.

14   A.    We live on the Maddox Ranch that covers 998 acres of land in San Saba and Llano Counties.

15         We have lived on this property for over fifty (50) years. With the help of the Federal Land

16         Bank, Roddy and I purchased the Ranch fifty years ago. We worked hard and paid off the

17         property in thirty-five (35) years.         Attached to my testimony is Exhibit RBM-1, which is a

18          screen shot ofthe interactive map provided by Oncor2 that shows the three tracts that includes

19         our Ranch in relation to the proposed route for Link J33.               I have not altered this map in any

20         way other than to outline the impacted tracts for ease of reference.

21




     2 httDS://www. oncor.com/content/oncorwww/us/en/home/about-us/transmission-svstems/current-transmission-line-

                                                                                                        Page 2 of 10
  1   Q.   WHAT IS THE TERRAIN LIKE ON THE RANCH?

 2   A.   The land is on a bedrock of granite. Our property has a lot of underground granite ledges

 3        that surface in various locations on the Ranch. There is an outcropping of the granite, for

 4        example, between our home and the barn. The terrain of the Ranch would not be considered

 5        soft rolling hills like you might find in other parts of the area. We have a very rocky high

 6        hill on the property and granite ledges throughout the property. I'll note that the land that

 7        our house is built on is probably the smoothest land on the Ranch.

 8   Q.   WHAT IS THE SIGNIFICANCE OR IMPORTANCE OF THIS PROPERTY TO

 9        YOU AND YOUR FAMILY.

10   A.    As I mentioned earlier, owning a ranch, along with the work that comes with it, was our

11         dream. We started with very little and through hard work, we saved and paid for this

12         Ranch. Roddy and I raised two sons on the Ranch, as well as six other boys that we helped

13         raise. Four ofthese boys graduated from Cherokee High School, as did our two sons. This

14         land is our primary legacy to hand down to our sons and their families.

15   Q.    WHO LIVES ON THE PROPERTY NOW?

16   A.    Roddy and I live full-time on the Ranch. We consider the Ranch our residence. Our sons

17         often visit and we have family gatherings throughout the year.

18   Q.    WHAT HABITABLE STRUCTURES DO YOU HAVE ON THE RANCH?

19   A.    We have our home that was built forty-seven (47) years ago where Roddy and I live. The

20         house is a white limestone ranch-style one-story 2,600 sq. ft. house. It includes three (3)

21         bedrooms, 24 baths, a large kitchen, and dining room/living room where we often gather

22         with up to thirty or so people at a time.

23

 5   Q.   WOULD        YOU     LOOK     AT     EXHIBIT         RBM-1   ATTACHED                   TO       YOUR

 6        TESTIMONY? THERE IS A BLUE SQUARE MARKED IN TRACT 1502. IS

 7        THAT THE LOCATION OF YOUR HOUSE?

 8   A.   No, it is not. I'm not sure what that square is supposed to represent; it was simply on the

 9        Oncor map.

10   Q.   ARE THERE OTHER HABITABLE STRUCTURES ON THE RANCH?

11   A.   Yes. We have two hunting cabins located on the Ranch. The North Pasture Cabin is located

12        in the north part of the property and is approximately one (1) mile north of our house. The

13        other cabin is located in the southern part of the Ranch approximately two (2) miles south

14        of our house and is known as the South Pasture Cabin. We use these cabins for hunters

15        who purchase deer or turkey leases. In the northern part ofthe Ranch, we have a barn that

 3        Ranch.

 6   Q.   WHAT OPERATIONS DO YOU HAVE ON THE RANCH?

 7   A.   In addition to being our full time residence, we currently raise cattle. We started out with

 8        cattle, hogs, sheep, and turkeys. Over time, we came to realize that this land was best

 9        conditioned for cattle - especially given the granite bed and outcroppings.

10   Q.   WHAT OTHER OPERATIONS DO YOU HAVE ON THE RANCH?

11   A.   We have wild turkeys, wild hogs, coyotes and other wildlife that live on the Ranch. As a

12        result, we offer and sell deer and turkey leases during hunting seasons. As I mentioned

13        earlier, we have two hunting cabins to accommodate hunters during the hunting seasons.

14        Our sons, grandsons, and even our great grandsons hunt wildlife on the Ranch, as well.

15


                                                                                         Page 5 of 10
  1   Q.       DO YOU HAVE ANY WATER WELLS ON THE RANCH?

 2   A.       Yes, we do. We have seven (7) wells located around the Ranch. Because our land is on a

 3            granite bed, the wells are fairly shallow. We use windmills to pump water from some of

 4            our water wells, and others, we use electric pumps to push or lift water from the well to the

 5            surface.

 6   Q.       ARE THERE ANY OTHER BODIES OF WATER THAT RUN THROUGH THE

 7            RANCH?
 8   A.       Yes, we have two creeks that run through our Ranch - Red Mountain Branch and Pecan

 9            Creek. Each of these waterways start separately at the north part of our property and then

10            join together on the south end of the Ranch. Then, they run all the way under Highway 71

11            near Llano. These creeks and springs contribute to the watershed that serves our Ranch

12            and this area. Also, since the Ranch has a lot of rough terrain, we catch water in stock

13            tanks and ponds.

14                       IV.     CONCERNS AND OBJECTIONS TO LINK J33

15   Q.       LET'S NOW TURN TO YOUR CONCERNS ABOUT LINK J33 THAT IS

16            CURRENTLY PROPOSED TO CROSS THE RANCH. CAN YOU LIST YOUR

17            CONCERNS ABOUT THIS LINK?

18   A.       Yes. Our concerns are:

19        •   The current proposed route for J33 will cross along the northern part of our Ranch which

20            impacts its use and will harm the outdoor uses that are so important to us.

21        •   The proposed route will significantly devalue our land and our legacy to our sons.

22        •   Any construction on granite will take a lot oftime, effort, and likely explosives and digging

23            that will disrupt our cattle operations and wildlife on the property.


                                                                                              Page 6 of 10
  1        •   There are potential risks to our water wells and creeks that run through the Ranch that could

 2            harm our cattle, wildlife, and us, as full-time residents on the Ranch.

 3   Q.       CAN YOU EXPLAIN YOUR FIRST CONCERN?

 4   A.       Yes. We tried a couple of times during the public hearings to get confirmation on the

 5            proposed route for Link J33. And both times, we received different answers. But, based

 6            on the Oncor map, as shown in Exhibit RBM-l, I believe that Link J33 will cut through

 7            along the north edge of our property. It isn't clear to us whether the Link would be on the

 8            property line or within the northern part of our land. If it' s the latter, then it will slice our

 9            property into two parts. It is not clear, as I understand that even after the Commission sets

10            the route, the details of this route can change.

11   Q.       WHY DOES THAT CONCERN YOU?

12   A.       We are concerned because cutting a 200-foot easement along the width of the northern

13            portion of our Ranch will disrupt our cattle operations based on how we rotate and graze

14            our cattle and disrupt the landscape and aesthetics of our Ranch. It will also disrupt the

15            wildlife as current vegetation where they live will be eliminated along and around the wide

16            easement. In practical terms, to us, it means that the wildlife will flee from our Ranch,

17            which will then impact our hunting leases and family hunting.

18   Q.       LET'S     TURN       TO    YOUR       SECOND         CONCERN         RELATED         TO     THE

19            DEVALUATION OF YOUR PROPERTY VALUE

20   A.       Having a 200-foot easement run along or inside our northern property line, along with the

21            unsightly and large towers to support the 765kV line, will hurt and harm the value of our

22            property once built. We worked hard to get this Ranch and achieve our dream. And, as I

23            mentioned, the Ranch is our legacy to hand down to our sons and their families. There is



                                                                                                  Page 7 of 10
  1        no conceivable way that the value of our Ranch will not be impacted, and we certainly

 2        won't be made whole with proceeds from condemnation. Having lived in this area for

 3        most of my life, I am certain that running this transmission line on the northern part of our

 4        Ranch will min the value of this Ranch.

 5   Q.   YOU RAISED A THIRD CONCERN ABOUT THE CONSTRUCTION AND USE

 6        OF EXPLOSIVES ON THE RANCH. CAN YOU PLEASE EXPLAIN?

 7   A.   Construction of this transmission line over our property is not going to be easy. As I

 8        mentioned earlier, our ranch is on hard rocky granite. Living on this property for so long,

 9        I am certain that building the kind of structure needed to support the 765kV transmission

10        line will take additional effort since the topography is not smooth or even (except around

11        our house). To us, then, that means that there will be a significant excavation process to

12        break up the granite formations to level the ground enough to support the tall bridge

13        structures that will support the transmission line. That type of excavation could include

14        the use of explosives, but it will most definitely require destructive construction. With

15        excavation along the width of our Ranch, this type of construction will impact our cattle

16        operations, as we really will have few places on the Ranch to move them that will not be

17        impacted by the construction and/or explosives. It will also impact all of the wildlife that

18        live on our Ranch - they willleave the area, and it is hard for me to believe that they can

19        or will all return once the construction is complete.     The impact of construction will

20        inevitably impact our ability to provide hunting leases and impact our use of the land.




                                                                                         Page 8 of 10
  1   Q.   FINALLY, YOU MENTIONED A CONCERN ABOUT YOUR WATER WELLS

 2        AND WATER SUPPLY. PLEASE EXPLAIN.

 3   A.   Water is so precious as a natural resource for us and our community. Our concern is that

 4        given that the water wells and creeks that flow through our Ranch run through and over

 5        granite, any construction that changes the topography of the land will impact the wells and

 6        creeks. Less flow of water means less water for our own personal use, as well as less water

 7        for our cattle and wildlife. A second concern is that there is likely to be sediment runoff

 8        (eroded soil that could clog the waterways or wells) and chemical leaching (such as cement

 9        or paint). I'm not claiming to be a scientist, but Roddy and I understand the delicacy of

10        our land and waterways. Any construction will impact our soil and could cause runoffs

11        where none existed before.     The types of towers that Oncor proposes to use will be

12        supported in cement and covered with paint - both of which can have run-off that flows

13        into our water.

14                             V.    CONCLUSION AND REQUEST

15   Q.   MRS.     MADDOX,          WHAT     ARE      RODDY       AND      YOU     ASKING       THE

16        ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES AND THE COMMISSION TO DO?

17   A.   We are asking that Link J33 not be used as part of the final route approved for this

18        transmission line.   We love our Ranch and we do not want to see it desecrated in the

19        manner that Link J33 will. Our Ranch is important to our family and to our sons' families;

20        it is important as we run cattle operations as a means of livelihood; it is important to the

21        wildlife that live on it; it has waterways and water wells that are important to our cattle,

22        wildlife, and surrounding areas; and it is important to the area as we maintain clean ways

23        of living that do not affect our watershed or the wildlife. We do not wish this dilemma on



                                                                                         Page 9 of 10
 1        anyone else, but we do hope there is a better route or a better way to accomplish what needs

2        to be done to get power to the folks who need it.

3   Q.   DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY?

4   A.   Yes, it does.
